messages.author: 363861a949524eb3
messages.subject: bug report: aes_string + geom_hex + facet_wrap
parts:
The documentation for facet_wrap has this as a first example:

d <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price, fill = ..density..)) +
xlim(0, 2) + stat_binhex(na.rm = TRUE) + opts(aspect.ratio = 1)
d + facet_wrap(~ color)


When replacing aes() with aes_string() , using facet_wrap() triggers
an error when
rendering the plot:

d <- ggplot(diamonds, aes_string("carat", "price", fill =
"..density..")) +
xlim(0, 2) + stat_binhex(na.rm = TRUE) + opts(aspect.ratio = 1)

> d + facet_wrap(~ color)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'color' not found

L.

On Wed, Feb 17, 2010 at 3:34 AM, lgautier <lgau...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> The documentation for facet_wrap has this as a first example:
>
> d <- ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price, fill = ..density..)) +
>       xlim(0, 2) + stat_binhex(na.rm = TRUE) + opts(aspect.ratio = 1)
>     d + facet_wrap(~ color)
>
>
> When replacing aes() with aes_string() , using facet_wrap() triggers
> an error when
> rendering the plot:
>
> d <- ggplot(diamonds, aes_string("carat", "price", fill =
> "..density..")) +
>       xlim(0, 2) + stat_binhex(na.rm = TRUE) + opts(aspect.ratio = 1)

That's because in aes_string you need to explicitly specify all the
aesthetic names: aes_string(x = "carat", y = "price", fill =
"..density..")
